sources_considered.why: Contemporary professional literature on radiological reports, manual review and clinical NLP.
Contemporary primary research on converting free-text radiology reports into structured information.
Readable full text discussing patient histories and the radiologist's wider workflow; originally published in 2021, so used as context.
Primary evidence of successful convolutional-network clinical text classification, qualifying a broad reading of less suited.
read_page returned a browser check; the Europe PMC full-text endpoint was readable.

evidence_items.publisher: Journal of the American College of Radiology; abstract hosted by PubMed
evidence_items.explanation: The review describes radiological reports as commonly unstructured and their manual review as costly. It supports the textual-information component of radiology work, but does not establish the architectural comparison.

The paper documents difficulties with clinical free text and evaluates a transformer approach. Its task is report structuring; it does not directly compare convolutional image interpretation with reasoning over patient histories.

evidence_items.publisher: Pediatric Radiology; full text hosted by Europe PMC
evidence_items.locator: Section Information technology support and shortcomings
evidence_items.explanation: The professional discussion describes histories, previous examinations and reports as parts of radiological workflow, and explains their diagnostic relevance. It predates the selected target period.

evidence_items.publisher: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making; full text hosted by Europe PMC
evidence_items.locator: Results, Results of the clinical text classification paradigm
evidence_items.explanation: This earlier report shows convolutional networks successfully classifying clinical text, including smoking status and fractures. It qualifies a blanket claim of text unsuitability, but does not demonstrate broad clinical-history reasoning or compare text with image tasks.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved study directly establishes the claimed relative suitability across image interpretation, patient-history reasoning and unstructured-text understanding.
Evidence about report extraction does not establish capability for reasoning over a patient's full clinical history.
The strongest retrieved description of history integration predates the selected observation window.
